title: An AI Company Wanted to Buy My Reporting Notes
key_facts: Handshake, founded in 2014 as a job-search platform for college students, contacted the writer on LinkedIn seeking reporting notes, drafts and edits.
Handshake offered $1,000 per "case" of at least 50 documents in three file types.
The draft contract gave Handshake a non-exclusive, royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, transferable and sublicensable licence while the writer kept ownership.
Handshake added an AI-training division in 2025 that hit $1 billion in gross revenue within fifteen months, working with eight AI labs.
Handshake chief communications officer Stephen Rocco Rodi confirmed the offer came from its document licensing program.
Lawyer Justin Nelson of Susman Godfrey said the contract meant giving them free ability to do whatever they want forever.
quote_evidence: Handshake offered a thousand dollars per case.
Ethically, I could see no reason to take the deal.
Each set of reporting documents would be considered a “case,” the message explained, and each case needed to have at least fifty documents, three file types, and a variety of document lengths.
why_it_matters_hint: AI companies are now paying professionals for their working papers, not just finished work.
notes: First-person account; the author is identified in the text only as Jules.
